design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (utility_pass_through_billing) — draw: draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5, 5]; late fee 5, refund 5.

WHY A GOOD TEST. Frances E. Holloway moved off site A-219 on 2026-09-22; her account is final_billed with a 750.00 credit built from a cashier's check (2026-09-29), her mailed check for the September statement (2026-10-02) and her daughter's portal bank payment for the final statement (2026-10-06). She asks for the overpayment back by check. The refund rule says 'A credit balance is not refunded until a late fee stands on the account for every statement whose unpaid amount at the end of its grace period reached the late-fee minimum.' The September statement (159.61, due 2026-09-21) was unpaid at the end of grace (2026-09-26) and no late fee is on the account, so the agent must first post the late fee (5 factors) and then work out the refund (5 factors: two risk-based holding periods, a true-up reserve rate and base for the estimated final read, and a tenure refund limit), handing the request to the resident.

SCOPE. Task 0 occupies the estimated read, usage charge and final-statement prepayment policies and tools; task 1 claims utility_ext_statement_late_fee (post_late_fee_5fe5b1d1) and utility_ext_final_credit_refund (request_credit_refund_3a7a9c57). Together the two tasks cover all five extended policies with disjoint tools.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root utility_ext_final_credit_refund (owner=user, on_request) <- utility_ext_statement_late_fee (agent, state_due); edge value_input, gate credit, state form, negated direction ('not refunded until'); false at opening: no utility_late_fee row although the 2026-09 statement was unpaid at grace end (first payment 2026-09-29). Exactly one write in the difficulty books a utility late fee (post_late_fee_5fe5b1d1). Order: late fee (step 8), refund (step 10). Skipping the late fee gives refund 566.05 instead of 403.28. user_scenario names no prerequisite; tools validate none.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Late fee (utility_late_fee): utility_evt_late_fee gate utility_grace_ended — anchor the statement due date 2026-09-21 (utility_ledger.due_date), 5 calendar grace days counted from the day after, fee no earlier than 2026-09-27 (exclusive); handling 2026-10-09 satisfies it; just before: 2026-09-26 fails. Unpaid at grace end 159.61 >= minimum 10.00. Courtesy waivers do not arise (only while the account is active). Refund (utility_credit_refund): utility_agg_account_settlement and utility_final_billing carry no gate for refunds (policy_scope); the account is final_billed; the base 'refunded by check ... at closing' clause is superseded by the refund rule's holding/limit sentence (declared overwrite).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. One account 974155f9-e417-46ea-ac91-6dcf6873e9eb. Late-fee object: the 2026-09 statement (usage 86.26 on the estimated 2026-08-22 read, fixed 70.10, admin 3.25). Refund object: the credit after the fee, 746.84; held items: the most recent personal check (2026-10-02, 159.61) and the most recent portal bank payment (2026-10-06, 118.33); the cashier's check is never held; reserve base: the 2026-09 and 2026-10 water usage charges (two estimated reads within two months).

FACTOR CARD. Late fee: basis 6 percent of 159.61 = 9.58 (baseline flat 10.00), first-lateness share 0.50, tenure share 0.80, payment-risk share 1.10 (lease late fee 2026-06-07), closed-lease share 0.75; result 3.16, baseline 10.0. Refund: check hold 10 days (baseline 5), bank hold 4 days (baseline 2), reserve rate 0.50 (baseline 0), reserve base 131.24 (baseline latest charge 44.98), limit 1,000.00 (baseline 250.00); result 403.28, baseline 250.0. Per-factor baseline results are in factor_sensitivity. Cross-difficulty: lease ledger late fee, returned payments (none), automatic drafts (none), lease status and accepted notice. Multi-source: check hold (utility late fee AND lease late fee, and no returned payment), risk share (lease late fee and no return), bank hold (no draft and at most one bank payment).

WORLD. Fourteen monthly cycles priced under the extended pricing (one occupant, single-section bounds 3.00/10.00); the 2026-08-22 and 2026-09-22 reads estimated per the estimate rule at their statement runs (15.28 and 10.76) and priced as first and second estimates; monthly personal-check payments; lease month-to-month, June 2026 rent paid late with the 35.00 minimum late fee, notice accepted 2026-08-17 for 2026-09-22 (36 days, above 30), September rent prorated 22/30, deposit refunded 2026-10-05.

PERSONA. Chatty, slightly flustered retiree; volunteers the goal and her three payments; credentials and mailing address on request; passive consent to the late fee and to a partial refund; submits the refund for the amount given and ends.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate/verify; read account, ledger, lease, lease requests, lease ledger; post late fee 3.16 on 2026-09; compute refund 403.28; hand over the refund request.

VERIFICATION. Authoring code (deleted after use) replayed gold with the real tools and evaluated each compute through check_compute's DSL at handling time: fee 3.16, refund 403.28. Per-task gates run green.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the published rules: the refund rule's prerequisite sentence and the ledger (September statement unpaid on 2026-09-26, no late fee) lead to the late-fee rule; its ladders with the ledger and lease data give 3.16; the refund rule's holds, reserve and limit give 403.28. Revision log: the reserve base first summed charges dated in the last whole month, which equalled the latest charge in this world (decorative); widened to the last two months.
user_scenario: You are Frances E. Holloway, seventy-eight. For seventeen years you lived on site A-219 at Bluebonnet Ridge in Conroe, Texas; on September 22 you moved into Willowcrest Senior Living, and the dealer who bought your old home hauled it off the site that same day. It is the afternoon of October 9 and you are calling the resident desk about your old water account. You think you have overpaid it, and you would like whatever extra is there sent back to you as a check. In a slightly flustered, chatty way you explain how it happened: on September 29 your daughter Joanne drove you to the office and you left a cashier's check for $750.00 to cover your last water bills; you had also mailed a personal check for the September bill before the move; and then Joanne, seeing the final bill online, paid it from her bank account through the resident portal. You are not sure of the other amounts and say you'd rather the desk look them up. You want the refund handled on this call, and you understand you'll put the refund request in yourself through the portal once the agent tells you the amount; you don't name an amount yourself. You first give your phone number, 936-555-0136. When asked to verify you give your date of birth, June 2, 1948 (1948-06-02); if they want something else, the last four of your Social Security number are 2287. You don't know any account numbers. If the agent asks where the check should go, you say the new address is already on your profile, 2715 Willowcrest Ln Apt 114, Conroe, TX 77304, and that's where it should be mailed. If the agent tells you that a late fee or any other charge has to go on the account first, you sigh that the move was hectic and say all right, go ahead. If the agent tells you that only part of the credit can be refunded today and the rest stays on the account for now, you say that's fine as long as you know what's coming. When the agent sets up the refund request for you and gives you the amount, you submit it for exactly that amount and read back the reference number you get. After that you thank the agent warmly and hang up; you don't raise anything else.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A utility late fee may be charged only after the grace period has ended, counted from the statement due date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the due date, and the fee may be posted no earlier than the day after the last grace day.

boundary_check.just_before: Due date 2026-09-21 plus 5 grace days ends 2026-09-26; on 2026-09-26 the fee may not yet be posted.
boundary_check.at_boundary: From 2026-09-27 (the day after the last grace day, exclusive boundary) the fee may be posted; the handling date 2026-10-09 is later, and the extended rule posts it in the month after the statement month (October).

late_fee_repeat_share (parameter): Evidence: no utility_late_fee row in twelve months. Value 0.50. Tier taken: 'no utility late fee posted in the last twelve months'. Baseline ({"repeat_share": "1.0"}) would give result 6.32.

late_fee_tenure_share (parameter): Evidence: service_start_date 2009-05-15, 208 whole months. Value 0.80. Tier taken: 'service began 120 or more whole months before the handling date'. Baseline ({"tenure_share": "1.0"}) would give result 3.95.

late_fee_risk_share (parameter): Evidence: lease late fee 2026-06-07 (lease cross-difficulty), no returned payment on lease or utility ledgers. Value 1.10. late_fee_closed_lease_share (parameter): Evidence: lease status closed, notice to vacate accepted (lease cross-difficulty). Value 0.75. Tier taken: 'the lease has closed and a notice to vacate was accepted on it'. Baseline ({"closed_share": "1.0"}) would give result 4.22.
Non-factor bindings: stmt_usage 86.26, stmt_fixed 70.10, stmt_admin 3.25, stmt_charges 159.61; result 9.58 x 0.5 x 0.8 x 1.1 x 0.75 = 3.1614 -> 3.16.
